newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers shares brighten on Russian support.
newsitem.headline: De Beers shares brighten on Russian support.

text.p: Encouraging statements from Russia supporting a trade deal with De Beers buoyed the diamond giant's shares in strong volumes on Friday, dealers said.
They added that a robust overnight Wall Street was offering substantial support to the whole equity market.
Having touched a day's high of 131 rand, De Beers added 175 cents to 130.25 rand by 1125 GMT, with 218,800 shares trading.
Earlier on Friday the head of Russia's Almazy-Rossii Sakha said that the lack of a diamond pact with De Beers would spur illegal diamond sales. This could destabilise the market.
Shortly afterwards Russian president Boris Yeltsin's spokesman said that the government was not against a deal.
This follows De Beers' ultimatum on Wednesday that the Russians sign a new deal by December 31 or De Beers would cease to buy diamonds from Russia under its old agreement.

"It's on the Russian statements which are being taken as very encouraging. We're unlikely to see De Beers fall as far as it did on Wednesday. It really got a bit of a shake-up but bounced right back," one dealer said.
"It was very much overdone and now it's coming back. Wall Street is giving a lot of encouragement too," he added.
The move by De Beers to force the Russians into action sank the group's shares on Thursday. The stock fell to 121.75 rand from an opening price of 128 rand.
